questions.question_text:
Consider a memory system with 1M bytes of main memory and 16K bytes of cache
memory. Assume that the processor generates 20-bit memory address, and the cache
block size is 16 bytes. If the cache uses direct mapping, how many bits will be
required to store all the tag values? [Assume memory is byte addressable, 1K=210,
1M=220 .]
questions.subtopic: Memory hierarchy: cache, main memory and secondary storage
questions.explaination: With block size $16 = 2^4$ bytes, block offset is 4 bits. Cache size is $16\text{ KB} = 2^{14}$ bytes, so number of cache lines is $2^{14}/2^4 = 2^{10} = 1024$, requiring 10 line index bits. The tag bits per line are $20 - (10 + 4) = 6$ bits. For all $2^{10}$ lines, total tag bits required are $6 \times 2^{10}$.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a memory system with 1M bytes of main memory and 16K bytes of cache memory. Assume that the processor generates 20-bit memory address, and the cache block size is 16 bytes. If the cache uses direct mapping, how many bits will be required to store all the tag values? [Assume memory is byte addressable, $1\text{K}=2^{10}, 1\text{M}=2^{20}$.]

questions.question_text:
A processor has 64 general-purpose registers and 50 distinct instruction types. An
instruction is encoded in 32-bits. What is the maximum number of bits that can be
used to store the immediate operand for the given instruction?
ADD R1, #25 // R1 = R1 + 25
questions.explaination: To represent 50 distinct instruction opcodes, $\lceil \log_2 50 \rceil = 6$ opcode bits are required. Specifying one destination register among 64 general-purpose registers requires $\lceil \log_2 64 \rceil = 6$ bits. In a 32-bit instruction word, the remaining bits for the immediate field are $32 - (6 + 6) = 20$ bits.

questions.question_text:
A computer has two processors, 𝑀1 and 𝑀2. Four processes 𝑃1, 𝑃2, 𝑃3, 𝑃4 with CPU
bursts of 20, 16, 25, and 10 milliseconds, respectively, arrive at the same time and
these are the only processes in the system. The scheduler uses non-preemptive
priority scheduling, with priorities decided as follows:
• 𝑀1 uses priority of execution for the processes as, 𝑃1 > 𝑃3 > 𝑃2 > 𝑃4, i.e.,
𝑃1 and 𝑃4 have highest and lowest priorities, respectively.
• 𝑀2 uses priority of execution for the processes as, 𝑃2 > 𝑃3 > 𝑃4 > 𝑃1, i.e.,
𝑃2 and 𝑃1 have highest and lowest priorities, respectively.
A process 𝑃𝑖 is scheduled to a processor 𝑀𝑘, if the processor is free and no other
process 𝑃𝑗 is waiting with higher priority. At any given point of time, a process can
be allocated to any one of the free processors without violating the execution
priority rules. Ignore the context switch time. What will be the average waiting time
of the processes in milliseconds?
questions.explaination: At $t = 0$, $M_1$ takes highest priority process $P_1$ (burst 20) and $M_2$ takes $P_2$ (burst 16). At $t = 16$, $M_2$ frees up; among remaining processes $\{P_3, P_4\}$, $P_3$ has higher priority on $M_2$, so $P_3$ runs on $M_2$ ($t = 16$ to 41). At $t = 20$, $M_1$ frees up and executes $P_4$ ($t = 20$ to 30). Waiting times are: $P_1 = 0$, $P_2 = 0$, $P_3 = 16$, $P_4 = 20$. Average waiting time is $(0 + 0 + 16 + 20) / 4 = 36 / 4 = 9.00$ ms.

questions.question_text:
A packet with the destination IP address 145.36.109.70 arrives at a router whose
routing table is shown. Which interface will the packet be forwarded to?
questions.subtopic: Routing protocols: shortest path, flooding, distance vector and link state routing
questions.explaination: The destination address has third octet $109 = 01101101_2$. For /16, $145.36.0.0$ matches. For /17 ($128 = 10000000_2$), the leading bit is 0, so /17 does not match. For /18 ($64 = 01000000_2$), the first two bits are $01_2$, which matches $109$ ($01101101_2$). For /24, 255 does not match. By Longest Prefix Match, /18 (interface E3) is chosen.
questions.question_text_latex:
A packet with the destination IP address 145.36.109.70 arrives at a router whose routing table is shown below:

\begin{tabular}{|l|l|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Subnet Address} & \textbf{Subnet Mask (CIDR)} & \textbf{Interface} \\
\hline
145.36.0.0 & /16 & E1 \\
145.36.128.0 & /17 & E2 \\
145.36.64.0 & /18 & E3 \\
145.36.255.0 & /24 & E4 \\
Default & -- & E5 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

Which interface will the packet be forwarded to?

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐴 be a 2 × 2 matrix as given.
𝐴= [ 1
1
1
−1 ]
What are the eigenvalues of the matrix 𝐴13 ?
questions.explaination: The characteristic equation of $A$ is $\det(A - \lambda I) = (1 - \lambda)(-1 - \lambda) - 1 = \lambda^2 - 2 = 0$, so eigenvalues of $A$ are $\lambda_1 = \sqrt{2}$ and $\lambda_2 = -\sqrt{2}$. The eigenvalues of $A^{13}$ are $(\sqrt{2})^{13} = 2^6 \sqrt{2} = 64\sqrt{2}$ and $(-\sqrt{2})^{13} = -64\sqrt{2}$.

Consider the following four variable Boolean function in sum-of-product form
𝐹(𝑏3, 𝑏2, 𝑏1, 𝑏0) = ∑(0, 2, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12).
where the value of the function is computed by considering 𝑏3𝑏2𝑏1𝑏0 as a 4-bit
binary number, where 𝑏3 denotes the most significant bit and 𝑏0 denotes the least
significant bit. Note that there are no don’t care terms. Which ONE of the following
options is the CORRECT minimized Boolean expression for 𝐹?

options.D:
𝑏̅0𝑏̅2 + 𝑏̅3

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: Grouping minterms on a 4-variable K-map: minterms $\{0, 2, 8, 10\}$ form a 4-cell group giving $\overline{b}_2\overline{b}_0$; minterms $\{0, 4, 8, 12\}$ form a 4-cell group giving $\overline{b}_1\overline{b}_0$; remaining minterm 11 combines with 10 to give $b_3\overline{b}_2b_1$. Combining these essential prime implicants yields $\overline{b}_1\overline{b}_0 + \overline{b}_2\overline{b}_0 + b_1\overline{b}_2b_3$.

questions.question_text:
Let 𝐺(𝑉, 𝐸) be an undirected and unweighted graph with 100 vertices. Let 𝑑(𝑢, 𝑣)
denote the number of edges in a shortest path between vertices 𝑢 and 𝑣 in 𝑉. Let the
maximum value of 𝑑(𝑢, 𝑣), 𝑢, 𝑣∈𝑉 such that 𝑢≠𝑣, be 30. Let 𝑇 be any breadth-
first-search tree of 𝐺. Which ONE of the given options is CORRECT for every such
graph 𝐺?

options.A: The height of 𝑇 is exactly 15.
options.B: The height of 𝑇 is exactly 30.
options.C: The height of 𝑇 is at least 15.
options.D:
The height of 𝑇 is at least 30.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths
questions.explaination: The diameter of $G$ is $\text{diam}(G) = \max_{u,v} d(u, v) = 30$. For any BFS root $r$, the triangle inequality ensures that for the pair $(u, v)$ realizing the diameter, $30 = d(u, v) \le d(r, u) + d(r, v) \le 2 \times \text{height}(T)$. Hence, $\text{height}(T) \ge \lceil 30/2 \rceil = 15$.
questions.question_text_latex: Let $G(V, E)$ be an undirected and unweighted graph with 100 vertices. Let $d(u, v)$ denote the number of edges in a shortest path between vertices $u$ and $v$ in $V$. Let the maximum value of $d(u, v), u, v \in V$ such that $u \neq v$, be 30. Let $T$ be any breadth-first-search tree of $G$. Which ONE of the given options is CORRECT for every such graph $G$?

options_latex.C: The height of $T$ is at least 15.
options_latex.D: The height of $T$ is at least 30.

questions.subtopic: Regular and context-free languages, pumping lemma
questions.explaination: For $L_2$, $\alpha = a^k$ ($k \ge 1$). A string belongs to $L_2$ if and only if it starts with $a$, ends with $a$, and has length at least 3 ($a(a+b)^+a$), which is clearly regular. For $L_1$, the prefix $\alpha$ and suffix $\alpha$ must match over $\{a, b\}^+$, which requires unbounded memory to verify matching arbitrary binary strings, making $L_1$ non-regular.

Consider the following two languages over the alphabet $\{a, b\}$:
\[ L_1 = \{ \alpha\beta\alpha \mid \alpha \in \{a, b\}^+ \text{ AND } \beta \in \{a, b\}^+ \} \]
\[ L_2 = \{ \alpha\beta\alpha \mid \alpha \in \{a\}^+ \text{ AND } \beta \in \{a, b\}^+ \} \]
Which ONE of the following statements is CORRECT?

options_latex.B: $L_1$ is a regular language but $L_2$ is not a regular language.
options_latex.C: $L_1$ is not a regular language but $L_2$ is a regular language.
options_latex.D: Neither $L_1$ nor $L_2$ is a regular language.

options.D:
Neither 𝐿1 nor 𝐿2 are context-free languages.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: In $L_2$, rewrite $c^{m+n} = c^n c^m$ or generate using PDA by pushing $a$'s and $b$'s and popping on $c$'s ($c$'s match total count of $a$'s and $b$'s), which requires a single stack, so $L_2$ is context-free. In $L_1$, $a^m b^m c^m c^n$ simultaneously requires equality between powers of $a$ and $b$, plus matching with $c$, requiring two independent stack comparisons, making $L_1$ non-CFL.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE while computing First and Follow
during top down parsing by a compiler?

options.A: For a production 𝐴→𝜖, 𝜖 will be added to 𝐹𝑖𝑟𝑠𝑡(𝐴).
options.B:
If there is any input right end marker, it will be added to 𝐹𝑖𝑟𝑠𝑡(𝑆), where 𝑆 is the
start symbol.
options.C: For a production 𝐴→𝜖, 𝜖 will be added to 𝐹𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑜𝑤(𝐴).
options.D:
If there is any input right end marker, it will be added to 𝐹𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑜𝑤(𝑆), where 𝑆 is
the start symbol.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: By definition of FIRST and FOLLOW: if $A \to \epsilon$, then $\epsilon \in \text{FIRST}(A)$ (A is true). $\epsilon$ can never belong to any FOLLOW set (C is false). The right end marker (\$) is placed into $\text{FOLLOW}(S)$ for the start symbol $S$ to mark the end of input (D is true, B is false).

options_latex.C: For a production $A \to \epsilon$, $\epsilon$ will be added to $Follow(A)$.
options_latex.D: If there is any input right end marker, it will be added to $Follow(S)$, where $S$ is the start symbol.

dependencies {𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒→𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑦, 𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒→𝑜𝑤𝑛𝑒𝑟}.
The relation 𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚 is decomposed into two relations, 𝑡1(𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒, 𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑦) and
𝑡2(𝑛𝑎𝑚𝑒, 𝑜𝑤𝑛𝑒𝑟). Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

options.A: The relation 𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚 is NOT in BCNF.
options.B: The relations 𝑡1 and 𝑡2 are in BCNF.

questions.question_text:
𝐴= {0, 1, 2, 3, … } is the set of non-negative integers. Let Ϝ be the set of functions
from 𝐴 to itself. For any two functions, 𝑓1, 𝑓2 ∈Ϝ, we define
(𝑓1⨀𝑓2)(𝑛) = 𝑓1(𝑛) + 𝑓2(𝑛)
for every number 𝑛 in 𝐴. Which of the following is/are CORRECT about the
mathematical structure (Ϝ, ⨀)?

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: Addition on non-negative integers is closed, associative, and commutative, so $\odot$ is associative and commutative. The identity function is $e(n) = 0$ for all $n \in A$, making $(\mathcal{F}, \odot)$ a commutative (Abelian) monoid. Inverses do not exist because negative function values are not in $A$, so it is not a group.

questions.question_text:
A disk of size 512M bytes is divided into blocks of 64K bytes. A file is stored in
the disk using linked allocation. In linked allocation, each data block reserves 4
bytes to store the pointer to the next data block. The link part of the last data block
contains a NULL pointer (also of 4 bytes). Suppose a file of 1M bytes needs to be
stored in the disk. Assume, 1K = 210 and 1M = 220. The amount of space in bytes
that will be wasted due to internal fragmentation is ______. (Answer in integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.explaination: Block size is $64\text{ KB} = 65536$ bytes, with 4 bytes for pointer, leaving $65536 - 4 = 65532$ bytes of file data per block. File size is $1\text{ MB} = 1048576$ bytes. Number of blocks needed is $\lceil 1048576 / 65532 \rceil = \lceil 16.001037 \rceil = 17$ blocks. The first 16 blocks store $16 \times 65532 = 1048512$ bytes, leaving $1048576 - 1048512 = 64$ bytes stored in the 17th block. Internal fragmentation in the last block is $65532 - 64 = 65468$ bytes.
questions.question_text_latex: A disk of size 512M bytes is divided into blocks of 64K bytes. A file is stored in the disk using linked allocation. In linked allocation, each data block reserves 4 bytes to store the pointer to the next data block. The link part of the last data block contains a NULL pointer (also of 4 bytes). Suppose a file of 1M bytes needs to be stored in the disk. Assume $1\text{K} = 2^{10}$ and $1\text{M} = 2^{20}$. The amount of space in bytes that will be wasted due to internal fragmentation is \_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in integer)

questions.question_text:
A computer has a memory hierarchy consisting of two-level cache (L1 and L2) and
a main memory. If the processor needs to access data from memory, it first looks
into L1 cache. If the data is not found in L1 cache, it goes to L2 cache. If it fails to
get the data from L2 cache, it goes to main memory, where the data is definitely
available. Hit rates and access times of various memory units are shown in the
figure. The average memory access time in nanoseconds (ns) is ________. (rounded
off to two decimal places)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Memory hierarchy: cache, main memory and secondary storage

questions.question_text:
In optimal page replacement algorithm, information about all future page references
is available to the operating system (OS). A modification of the optimal page
replacement algorithm is as follows:
The OS correctly predicts only up to next 4 page references (including the current
page) at the time of allocating a frame to a page.
A process accesses the pages in the following order of page numbers:
1, 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 1, 2, 4, 3, 1, 4.
If the system has three memory frames that are initially empty, the number of page
faults that will occur during execution of the process is ________ . (Answer in
integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.explaination: Simulating the 3 frames with 4-step lookahead: 1 (fault, [1]), 3 (fault, [1, 3]), 2 (fault, [1, 3, 2]). At page 4 (fault): window is (4, 2, 3, 1), farthest is 1, so replace 1 -> [4, 3, 2]. Pages 2, 3 hit. At page 1 (fault): window (1, 2, 4, 3), replace 3 -> [4, 1, 2]. Page 2, 4, 3 (fault): replace 1 -> [4, 3, 2]. Total faults = 3 compulsory + 3 replacement = 6 page faults.

questions.question_text:
Suppose a 5-bit message is transmitted from a source to a destination through a
noisy channel. The probability that a bit of the message gets flipped during
transmission is 0.01. Flipping of each bit is independent of one another. The
probability that the message is delivered error-free to the destination is ______ .
(rounded off to three decimal places)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Data link layer: framing, error detection, Medium Access Control, Ethernet bridging
questions.explaination: For each bit, the probability of correct transmission without flipping is $1 - 0.01 = 0.99$. Since all 5 bit transmissions are mutually independent, the probability that all 5 bits are transmitted error-free is $(0.99)^5 = 0.95099 \approx 0.951$.

questions.question_text:
Suppose a message of size 15000 bytes is transmitted from a source to a destination
using IPv4 protocol via two routers as shown in the figure. Each router has a defined
maximum transmission unit (MTU) as shown in the figure, including IP header.
The number of fragments that will be delivered to the destination is ________ .
(Answer in integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: At Router-1, max payload per fragment is $\lfloor (5000 - 20) / 8 \rfloor \times 8 = 4976$ bytes. 15000 bytes payload is fragmented into payloads of 4976, 4976, 4976, and 72 bytes (4 fragments). At Router-2 ($\text{MTU} = 3000$, max payload $\lfloor 2980/8 \rfloor \times 8 = 2976$ bytes), each of the three 4976-byte fragments splits into 2 fragments ($2976 + 2000$), yielding $3 \times 2 = 6$ fragments. The 72-byte fragment passes through intact. Total delivered fragments = $6 + 1 = 7$.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: First find normalizing constant $C$: $\int_1^4 C x^2 \, dx = C \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_1^4 = C \frac{64 - 1}{3} = 21C = 1 \implies C = \frac{1}{21}$. Then $P(2 \le x \le 3) = \int_2^3 \frac{1}{21} x^2 \, dx = \frac{1}{21} \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_2^3 = \frac{27 - 8}{63} = \frac{19}{63} \approx 0.30158 \approx 0.302$.

The function `foo` counts 1 whenever two consecutive adjacent elements differ ($S[0] 
eq S[1]$), plus 1 for the base case `size == 1`. In array $A = \{0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 0, 0, 1, 1\}$, adjacent transitions where $A[i] 
eq A[i+1]$ occur at indices: $0 	o 1$ ($0 
eq 1$), $1 	o 2$ ($1 
eq 2$), $4 	o 5$ ($2 
eq 0$), and $6 	o 7$ ($0 
eq 1$). There are 4 such differences, plus 1 returned at `size == 1`, giving $4 + 1 = 5$.

The loop inspects each node following the head of `L1` (`ptr1->next`). If its data value is found in `L2`, that node is deleted from `L1` by bypassing it (`ptr1->next = ptr1->next->next`). Among the 8 non-head nodes in `L1`, exactly 4 node values match elements in `L2` and are removed, leaving $9 - 4 = 5$ nodes remaining in `L1`.

For $n = 14362$, the first loop computes $t = 10000$. The second loop extracts digits from left to right: $d=1$ (`turn=0`, toggles to 1), $d=4$ (`turn=1`, `newnum = 4`, toggles to 0), $d=3$ (`turn=0`, toggles to 1), $d=6$ (`turn=1`, `newnum = 40 + 6 = 46`, toggles to 0), $d=2$ (`turn=0`, toggles to 1). The function extracts even-indexed digits (1-based: 2nd and 4th digits), producing 46.

questions.question_text:
The maximum value of 𝑥 such that the edge between the nodes B and C is included
in every minimum spanning tree of the given graph is _________ . (answer in
integer)
questions.subtopic: Graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths
questions.explaination: By the cycle property of minimum spanning trees, an edge $e = (B, C)$ is included in every MST if and only if it is strictly lighter than the heaviest edge on every cycle containing $(B, C)$. Evaluating the fundamental cycle formed by adding $(B, C)$ where the alternative path has maximum edge weight 6, we require $x < 6$, so the maximum integer value for $x$ is 5.

questions.question_text:
In a double hashing scheme, ℎ1(𝑘) = 𝑘 mod 11 and ℎ2(𝑘) = 1 + (𝑘 mod 7) are
the auxiliary hash functions. The size 𝑚 of the hash table is 11. The hash function
for the i-th probe in the open address table is [ℎ1(𝑘) + 𝑖 ℎ2(𝑘)] mod 𝑚. The
following keys are inserted in the given order: 63, 50, 25, 79, 67, 24.
The slot at which key 24 gets stored is ___________. (Answer in integer)
questions.explaination: Hash values: key 63 at $63 \bmod 11 = 8$; key 50 at $50 \bmod 11 = 6$; key 25 at $25 \bmod 11 = 3$; key 79 at $79 \bmod 11 = 2$; key 67 has $h_1(67) = 1$, stores at 1. For key 24: $h_1(24) = 24 \bmod 11 = 2$ (collision with 79), $h_2(24) = 1 + (24 \bmod 7) = 1 + 3 = 4$. Probe $i=1$: $(2 + 4) \bmod 11 = 6$ (collision with 50). Probe $i=2$: $(2 + 8) \bmod 11 = 10$ (empty). Hence, key 24 is stored in slot 10.
